newsitem.title: PERU: Peru postpones vote on marriage-after-rape law.
newsitem.headline: Peru postpones vote on marriage-after-rape law.

text.p: The Peruvian Congress postponed until next week a vote on whether to repeal a 1924 law that allows rapists to go free if they marry their victims, legislators said early on Friday.

The bill, which has strong support of local women's groups, was to have been voted on early Friday but was rescheduled for vote next Thursday because of a backlog of other legislation, lawmakers said.
Congress' Justice Committee voted unanimously on Tuesday to eliminate the article in Peru's penal code, and the full Congress was expected to pass the legislation easily.
The reform will "allow the defence of women's rights against sexual violence," Beatriz Merino, president of Congress' women's committe and an opposition legislator said.
"Rapists will not remain unpunished just because they marry their victims. We are eliminating a judicial aberration," she said this week.
Women's groups say scores of Peruvian men take advantage of the law every year, particularly in poor and rural areas where rape is on the increase.
Peru had 4,500 cases of rape reported in 1995, but experts say only 10 to 30 percent of all cases are reported.
